mainEntity.name: What are common design considerations for an accessible in-law suite?

acceptedAnswer.text: Designing an accessible in-law suite involves incorporating features that support individuals with mobility challenges. Common considerations include wider doorways (at least 36 inches), zero-threshold entries, grab bars in bathrooms, roll-in showers, and accessible kitchen layouts with adjustable counters. A practical tradeoff is balancing aesthetic preferences with functional requirements. While some accessible features might appear more utilitarian, integrating universal design principles can create a space that is both visually appealing and highly functional for all. Discussing specific accessibility needs with your designer or contractor early in the process is crucial.
acceptedAnswer.description: Accessible in-law suites require wider doorways, zero-threshold entries, grab bars, roll-in showers, and accessible kitchen layouts. Balancing aesthetics with functional needs is a key design consideration.
